This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the award dated 24.8.2019 passed in MACC No.6/2017 by MACT, Lav Kush Nagar, Chhatarpur seeking exoneration from liability to pay compensation and for reduction Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that FIR has been registered after two days of the incident and it has been registered against unknown vehicle.
Tribunal has wrongly held that accident occurred from offending vehicle just on the ground that insurance company has not lead any evidence in rebuttal.
It is also urged that delay in lodging the FIR has not been explained.
Owner and driver of the offending vehicle has also filed written statement and therein they have also pleaded that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the accident.
After referring to deposition of applicant witness, it is urged that injured has admitted that immediately after the accident, she became unconscious.

Further from deposition of applicant witnesses Brijesh Mishra and Guman Singh, it is not established that they witnessed the number of the offending vehicle and they have did not lodge the first information report mentioning the number of the offending vehicle.
As per deposition of applicant witnesses, owner and driver of the offending vehicle were not found on the site of the accident.
So far as claim filed by the Lrs of Rajdhar Pathak is concerned, that case has been disposed off on the basis of evidence recorded in that case.
Therefore, just on the basis of above, claim has been allowed, present claim petition cannot be allowed.
On above grounds, it is urged that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the case.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appeal filed by the appellant be allowed and insurance company be exonerated from liability to pay the compensation amount and impugned award be set aside.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to para 13 of the impugned award submits that Tribunal has itself held that claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
There is no evidence of any doctor and there is no PDC certificate on record.
Therefore, it cannot be said that claimant has suffered any permanent disability.
Still Tribunal has awarded 50% for loss of future earning capacity, which is contrary to law and no amount can be awarded under the head of loss of earning future capacity.

On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be reduced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents after referring to para 10 of impugned award submits that in the instant accident, one Rajdhar Pathak has expired and claim petition filed by LRs of Rajdhar Pathak, has been allowed after taking into consideration of deposition of Guman Singh.
It is urged that from evidence of applicant witnesses, it is clearly established that accident has been caused by the offending vehicle.
It is also urged that claimant remained hospitalized for a considerable period and she has also suffered various fractures and there are implants in the body of the claimant.
Therefore, Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation treating 50% loss of future earning capacity.
Hence, no reduction is required in the instant case and appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
5 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. Primary contention of the learned counsel for the appellant insurance company is that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the accident just to get the compensation.

It is correct that accident occurred on 17.11.2015 and FIR Ex.P/2 has been registered on 19.11.2015 on the basis of written report Ex.P/3 and report Ex.P/2 has been lodged against the unknown tractor.

But perusal of written report reveals that therein it is mentioned:-

sentences.text: Vide seizure memo Ex.P/7, glass of tractor light and black cover, broker rubber of tractor light and pieces were recovered from the scene of accident on 19.11.215.

Perusal of Ex.P/8 Panchnama reveals that broken pieces of light etc, which were recovered from the scene of accident vide Ex.P/7 seizure memo were tallied with the right side of old head light of offending vehicle seized vide seizure memo Ex.P/6 and upon tallying the same, it was found that left side head light of the tractor was new one and the right side is the old one.
Thus, from Panchanama E.P/8, it is established that broken pieces recovered from the scene of accident are similar to that of old right side head light of offending vehicle.

8. Perusal of written statement filed by owner and driver of offending vehicle reveals that therein,
they have not been clarified as to when the left side head light of offending vehicle was damaged and when it was replaced, especially, if it was not damaged in the accident, then, when and how it got damaged.
9. Perusal of deposition of applicant witness Guman Singh reveals that accident occurred in his presence and he has witnessed the incident.
There is nothing in his cross-examination so as to show that he reached the scene of accident after accident had taken place.

In this Court's opinion,
deposition of applicant witness Guman Singh stands corroborated from documentary evidence as discussed in the preceding paras.

Therefore, Guman Singh's testimony cannot be disbelieved and his statement cannot be discarded just on the ground that his name is not mentioned in the witness list of charge sheet E.P/1.
10.
Further, in the instant case, charge sheet has been filed after investigation into the instant accident against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Driver/owner of offending vehicle has filed written statement but therein there is no such specific pleadings that if accident did not occur from the tractor, then, why it has been falsely implicated in the case and if accident did not occur from the offending vehicle, then, where it was at the time of accident including the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, owner and driver of the offending vehicle did not appear before the Tribunal and they were proceeded ex-parte.
Thus, there is no evidence in rebuttal on behalf of the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

11. It is well established that in cases relating to claims under the Motor Vehicle Act, claimant has to prove his case by preponderance of probabilities and he is not required to prove his case beyond reasonable doubt.
In the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of discussion in the preceding paras, in this Court's opinion, claimants have proved their case by preponderance of probabilities.
12. Therefore, it cannot be said that Tribunal has erred in concluding that accident occurred from offending vehicle and it was being driven rashly and negligently by respondent no.1.

Hence, with Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Kamla Dwivedi on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174374807/
3 respect to above, findings recorded by the Tribunal are affirmed.

sentences.text: 13. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, in the instant case, evidently, no permanent disability certificate has been filed by the respondent/claimant and no doctor has been examined.
Thus, from evidence on record, it is not established that respondent/ claimant has filed any permanent disability certificate on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, learned counsel for the appellant is right when he contends that no amount can be awarded under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
In the instant case, tribunal has awarded Rs.2,52,000/- for loss of future earning capacity.
14. In the instant case, appellant has suffered fracture in the right ulna bone, left radius bone and femur bone etc..
Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- for attendant charges and for pain and suffering only.
15. In view of fractures suffered by the claimants\respondents, it could b e presumed that she was not able to work for at least 3 months.
Therefore, respondent\ claimant is entitled to receive Rs 12,000/- for loss of income during treatment period.
Further, respondent claimant is also entitled to receive Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/- for attendant /conventional /nourishing diet.

1 6 . Hence, in view of above, claimants are entitled to receive Rs.1,27,691/- (Rs.50,691/- for medical expenses Rs.12,000-/ for loss of income during treatment period Rs.15,000/- for attendant charges/nourishing diet etc. and Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering.)
17. Thus claimant is entitled to receive Rs.1,27,691/- whereas Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,12,691/- as compensation.
Hence, compensation amount is reduced by Rs.1,85,000/-.
Other findings of Tribunal shall remain intact.
If excess amount has been deposited by the appellant Insurance company then, it shall be entitled to recover the same from the claimants.
18. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed and disposed off accordingly.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Kamla Dwivedi on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174374807/
